Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM4201 : Nanobiotechnology { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Nanobiotechnology and Nanomaterials: Introduction to nanobiotechnology, Applications of nanobiotechnology, and Zero-dimensional, One-dimensional, Two-dimensional nanomaterials (2D), Three-dimensional nanomaterials (3D).
Module 2: Synthesis and Assembly of Nanomaterials: Synthesis of nanomaterials - Heterogeneous and Homogeneous nucleation, Self-assembled structure in a biological system, Nanocarrier, Biological nanocontainers, and Biosynthesis of nanomaterials - Bacterial Nanocellulose.
Module 3: Fabrication Techniques and Functionalization: BioMEMS, Lithography: Electron beam lithography, Focused-ion beam lithography, Scanning probe, Nanoimprint lithography, Functionalization of CNTs - Synthesis of CNTs and CNT-based biosensors.
Module 4: Advanced Applications in Sensing and Nanodevices: Biosensors, Fluorescence resonance energy transfer, Nanoparticle-based sensors, Nucleic acid based nanodevices, DNA nanotechnology, RNA nanotechnology and Bionanomotors

Course Objective

1 .

To study the nanoscale biological molecules and their applications
2 .

To understand the fabrication of nanostructureed devices
3 .

To obtain knowledge on nano sensors and nanodevices
4 .

To learn various biosynthesis techniques of nanomaterials

Course Outcome

1 .

Familiarize with various characterization techniques of the nanomaterials
Explain the fundamental concepts of biosynthesis of nanomaterials
Comprehend the structure and function of various nanoscale biomolecules
Gain knowledge of the synthesis and fabrication of nano-engineered materials
Understand the applications of nanomaterials in medical industry

Essential Reading

1 .

Mirkin, C.A. and Niemeyer, C.M., Nanotbiotechnology II: More concepts and Applications, Wiley

2 .

K.K. Jain, Nanobiotechnology in Molecular Diagnostics: Current Techniques and Applications, Horizon Bioscience

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Lamprecht, A., Nanotherapeutics: Drug Delivery Concepts in Nanoscience, Pan Stanford Publishing Pvt. Ltd

2 .

K.K. Jain, Nanobiotechnology in Molecular Diagnostics: Current Techniques and Applications, Horizon Bioscience

6800.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CH2210 : Chemical Reaction Engineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction: Reaction rate laws and stoichiometry Classifications of reactions order and molecularity of reaction and its determination, theory on reaction: collision theory and activated complex theory analysis of data. Isothermal Reactor Design: Design of Batch reactor (BR), continuous stirred tank reactor (CSTR), plug flow reactor (PFR), packed-bed reactor (PBR) for single ideal reactions, multiple reactions reaction mechanism and pathways introduction to enzyme kinetics. Non-isothermal reactors. Catalysts and catalytic reactions: classification of catalysts, catalyst deactivation, external diffusion effects on heterogeneous reactions, diffusion and reaction in solid catalysts general mechanism of catalytic reactions, adsorption isotherms. Multiphase reactions. Non-ideal Reactors: causes of non-ideality residence time distribution (RTD)- Measurements and characteristics of RTD, models for non-ideal reactors.

Course Objective

1 .

To train students how to analyze chemical reactors and reaction systems.
2 .

To provide practice at developing critical and creative thinking skills related to reaction engineering.
3 .

To enable students to analyze the kinetic data, and to estimate kinetic parameters.
4 .

To provide practice with computer software and simulation relating to chemical reaction engineering.

Course Outcome

1 .

Students will be able to
1. Design chemical reactors and processes using minimum amount of data
2. Design experiments to get optimum product yield and selectivity.
3. Increase capacity and/or selectivity and/or safety by improving/changing the reactor type/sequence and/or operating conditions

Essential Reading

1 .

H. S. Fogler, Elements of Chemical Reaction Engineering,, Prentice Hall , 5th Edition, 2016.

2 .

O. Levenspiel, Chemical Reaction Engineering, John Wiley & Sons , 3rd edition, 1999

Supplementary Reading

1 .

G. F. Froment, K. B. Bischoff and J. D. Wilde, Chemical Reactor Analysis and Design, John Wiley , 3rd edition, 2010

2 .

J. M. Smith, Chemical Engineering Kinetics, Mcgraw-Hills , 3rd edition, 1981

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : ER6071 : Instrumentation Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introducing Atmospheric Instrumentation, Stevenson’s Screen and its components, Temperature and Humidity measurements, Sling Psychometer, Explanation of Automatic Weather Station (AWS), demo of AWS installed at Department’s rooftop, Introducing Pocket Weather meter and other handheld weather instrument, Demo for recording observations using these handheld instruments, Introducing Different Atmospheric Instruments, e.g., Radar, SODAR, LiDAR, Solid State Sensors, Pressure measurements, wind measurements, rainfall measurement, Explaining the Research Publication, Demonstration of Microtop available at Department, Demonstration of Laser Precipitation Monitor available at Department, Demonstration of GPS Recorder available at Department, Demonstration of Lagrangian Model runs for plotting Back/forward air mass trajectories, Discussion about Clouds (Types, Identifications), Visit to various sites at NIT Rourkela Campus for recording weather observations using handheld instruments and plotting and analysis of observations collected, plotting and analysis of recorded observations, presentations of results obtained during observations recording and data collected by other Government agencies available for other sites in public domain.

Course Objective

1 .

To understand the working principles of various instruments.
2 .

To learn monitoring/measurements of parameters using atmospheric instrumentation.
3 .

Data analysis and depiction of results from these observations.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: Understanding the basic weather instruments and their working principles.
CO2: Learning the atmospheric measurements using hand-held instruments.
CO3: Understanding the planning and executing an experiment for weather measurement.
CO4: Data analysis and interpretation of in-situ observations.
CO5: Learning to produce a quality-controlled dataset ready for archiving in a database, including handling and storage of measured data.

Essential Reading

2 .

Harrison, G., Meteorological measurements and instrumentation., John Wiley & Sons , 2015

Supplementary Reading

1 .

World Meteorological Organization, (No-8): Guide to meteorological and oceanographic instruments,, WMO , 2010

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC3205 : Computer Organization & Architecture { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Computer Building Blocks: Overview and History of Computer, CPU, Memory, Input-Output Subsystems, Control Unit.

Module 2 :

Instruction Set Architecture: Instruction Execution Cycle, Instruction Set Types, Instruction Format, Addressing Modes, Instruction Set.
Module 3 :

Computer Arithmetic: Unsigned and Signed Number Representation, Fixed and Floating Point Representations, Integer Addition and Subtraction, Floating Point Arithmetic, Design of Arithmetic And Logic Unit (ALU).
Module 4 :

Processor Architecture: Components Of CPU, Pipelining, Parallel Processing, Multiprocessor System and Multi-Coring.
Module 5 :

Memory Design and Organization: Memory Technologies, Memory Organization, Cache Memory, Hierarchical Memory Organization.
Module 6 :

I/O And Peripherals: Input-Output Subsystems, Interrupts, Bus System, DMA, Synchronous Vs. Asynchronous I/O, External Storage.

Course Objective

1 .

To have a conceptual understanding on the basics organizational and architectural issues of a digital computer.
2 .

To study the instruction set architecture and computer arithmetic for designing an ALU.
3 .

To acquire knowledge on the basic memory design technologies and memory organizational issues of a computer.
4 .

To learn about various Input-Output subsystems and peripherals, and the interfacing techniques.

Course Outcome

1 .

Conceptualize the basics of organizational and architectural issues of a digital computer.
2 .

Ability to understand the design principles of Instruction Set Architecture and ALU.
3 .

Evaluate cost performance and design trade-offs in designing and constructing a computer processor.
4 .

Analyse performance issues in processor and memory design of a digital computer.
5 .

Gain knowledge on modern computer systems to solve real life practical and state of the art problems to serve VLSI industries.

7568.t: EE6248: Condition Monitoring of High Voltage Insulation in Power System Equipments
7568.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE6248 : Condition Monitoring of High Voltage Insulation in Power System Equipments { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-I: Introduction: Interconnection of HV Power System Components, Insulation coordination, Future insulation monitoring requirements. (2 Hrs)
Module-II: Introduction of Generation and Measurement of Testing Voltages: High Voltage DC Generation, High Voltage AC Generation, High Voltage Impulse Generation, Spark gap measurement, Potential dividers, other measuring device, Corona and gap discharge current measurement. (5 Hrs)
Module-III: Insulating Materials Utilized In Power-System Equipment: Review of insulating materials (Solid, Liquid and Gases and Vacuum), Characterization of insulation, Deterioration and failure insulation, Electrical breakdown and operating stresses, insulation applications. (4 Hrs)
Module-IV: Introduction to Electrical Insulation Design Concepts: Overview of insulation design requirements, Electric stress distributions in simple insulation systems, Electric stress control. (3 Hrs)
Module-V: Basic Methods for Insulation Assessment: Non-destructive electrical measurements, Physical and chemical diagnostic methods, (3 Hrs)
Module-VI: Sensors for Insulation Condition Monitoring: Ultra-high-frequency sensors, Optical-fibre sensors, sensors for PD measurements. (4Hrs)
Module-VII: Online Insulation Condition Monitoring Techniques: Problems with offline condition monitoring, Noise-mitigation, Non-electrical online condition monitoring, Acoustic/Electric PD location methods, Electrical online condition monitoring, Gas Insulated Substations, Lightning Phenomena, AI techniques for condition assessment, DGA. (8 Hrs)
Module-VIII: Insulation Testing on High Voltage Power System Equipment: Objective of HV testing, Test classification, Test procedure and Standards, Testing of HV measuring Devices, PD Test, Dielectric loss Test, Testing of HV Apparatus and Electrostatic Hazards. (7 Hrs)

Course Objective

1 .

To learn about the recent trends in condition monitoring and test technique of high voltage power system equipment
2 .

To understand the concept of basic methods for Insulation assessment with different sensors application.
3 .

To learn about the diagnostic method for condition monitoring of high voltage equipment and gas insulated systems.
4 .

To enable students, learning procedure to carry out health assessment studies for expensive power apparatuses.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1. Learn the basic concepts of condition monitoring of HV power system equipment
CO2. Understand practical techniques to generate and measure high-voltages (DC, AC, impulse).
CO3. Understand the functions of various types of equipment and major components used in electrical power systems
CO4. Apply appropriate electrical/physical/chemical test methods for insulation assessment
CO5. Have detailed knowledge of the various types of electrical/physical/chemical diagnostic measurements for insulation assessment in particular partial discharge detection, measurement, and characterization.
CO6. Able to develop skill to assess and interpret the diagnostic test results for health assessment concerning residual life enhancement and reliable operation before any catastrophic failure of power equipment occur.

Essential Reading

1 .

Nazar Hussain Malik, A. A. Al-Arainy, and Mohammad Iqbal Qureshi, Electrical Insulation in Power System, CRC Press, New York , 1971

2 .

Andrew R. Hilema, Insulation Coordination for Power Systems, CRC Press , 1991

Supplementary Reading

1 .

R.E. James and Q. Su, Condition Assessment of High Voltage Insulation in Power System Equipment, The Institution of Engineering and Technology, London, United Kingdom , 2008

2 .

D. Kind and K. Feser, High-Voltage Test Techniques, SAB Publications, 2nd edition , 1999

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PA4315 : Advanced Building Construction { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I
Space structures: Introduction to space structures, possibilities in different materials, types of space structures and possibilities in different materials to cover large spans. Assignment: physical models to be made for different space frame structures.
Module II
Shell & grid structures: General study of shell structures and folded plate structures in concrete, their types, construction aspects, merits and demerits etc. General study of grid structures and skeletal structures, space frames, domes, and others in steel, their types, construction aspects, merits and demerits etc. Assignment: physical models to be made for different shell and grid structural systems.
Module III
Suspension & Catenary structures: General study of suspension structures and catenary structures. Membrane and pneumatic structures: types, materials used, merits, demerits and examples.
Module IV
Temporary structures: Materials and techniques used, constructional aspects using timber and steel General study of construction techniques to cover large spans using short-length timber and laminated timber materials, lamella roofing, portal frames, slip-form construction.
Module V
High-rise buildings: Foundation, structural systems, and architectural design considerations Earthquakes and their effect on buildings, earthquake zones in India, architectural design considerations and constructional detailing for earthquake resistance.

Course Objective

1 .

1. To identify and apply appropriate construction systems and associated building materials for complex buildings, solving the large spans and unconventional structures.
2 .

2. To acquire knowledge for adopting newer structural systems in the construction industry.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Ability to interpret and classify complex structural typologies successfully.
2. Ability to use contemporary building materials in advanced construction.
3. Ability to analyse and execute large spans and unconventional structures.

Essential Reading

1 .

Chudley, R., Greeno, R., & Kovac, K., Chudley and Greeno's Building Construction Handbook., Routledge.

2 .

Salvadorri, M. G., and Heller, R. A., . Structures in Architecture (2nd Revised edition), NJ: Prentice Hall.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Emmitt, S., Barry's introduction to construction of buildings., John Wiley & Sons.

2 .

Beedle, L.S., Advances in Tall Buildings, Hoboken, NJ: Wiley.
